cards.text: Paul is writing to the church of God in Corinth, and he's just said God made them ministers of a new covenant, of the Spirit (2 Cor 1:1; 3:6). Now he looks back at the old one, engraved in letters on stone. He calls it the ministry of death.
But Paul says even that ministry of death came with glory. So much glory that the Israelites could not keep looking at one man's face.

cards.question: The old covenant on stone came with so much glory that the Israelites couldn't gaze at one man's face. Whose face was it?
Paul says the glory on Moses' face was there to stay.

cards.text: Now Paul starts building, friend. If the ministry of DEATH came with glory like that, then come on now, what about the ministry of the Spirit?

cards.question: The ministry of death came with glory. What does Paul say about the ministry of the Spirit?

answers.text: It will be even more glorious
It will be just as glorious
It will have no glory at all

cards.question: Paul sets the two side by side: the old ministry brings condemnation, and the new ministry brings ___.

cards.text: Paul says what was once glorious has no glory now next to the glory that surpasses it. That's a porch light at noon, friend: still on, still trying, and NOBODY can tell.

cards.question: Paul makes one more comparison. The old glory was fading away. What does he say the new glory does?

cards.text: So Paul is holding a hope THAT big. And he says it changes how they carry themselves.

cards.question: Since they have such a hope, Paul says they are very ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says they are not like Moses, and he points to what Moses would put over his face. Friend, back in my junk drawer days, the only thing covering MY face was dust.

cards.question: What would Moses put over his face?
Paul gives the reason Moses covered his face. What was it?

answers.text: To keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away
To keep the Israelites from being afraid to come near him
To keep his own eyes from the light of the glory

cards.text: But Paul says the Israelites' minds were closed. And to this day, the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant.

cards.question: Paul says that veil at the reading of the old covenant hasn't been lifted. Where is the only place it can be removed?
Even to this day, when Moses is read, Paul says a veil covers something. What does it cover?

cards.text: So is that veil stuck there for good? Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in the back of a drawer, so trust me, I LOVE what Paul says next.

cards.question: When does Paul say the veil is taken away?

answers.text: Whenever anyone turns to the Lord
Whenever the old glory fades out

cards.question: Paul says the Lord is the Spirit. What does he say is there wherever the Spirit of the Lord is?

cards.text: Then Paul brings it all home. No veil this time: we all, with unveiled faces, reflect the glory of the Lord.

cards.question: Paul says something is happening to all of us who reflect the glory of the Lord with unveiled faces. What is it?

answers.text: We are being transformed into His image
We are learning to hide it from others
We are slowly losing it like Moses

cards.question: Paul says the glory we reflect fades away, just like the glory on Moses' face.

cards.text: Moses' glory faded, but this glory keeps intensifying, and it comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit. Forget the porch light, friend. THIS is the sun coming up.

findings.problem: "he's just said God made them ministers of a new covenant" makes "them" read as the Corinthian church. In 2 Cor 3:6 the ministers are "us": Paul and those with him. The card states something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The right answer, "To keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away," uses the passage's own wording. It also echoes "fading away," which earlier cards already established (stop 1 cards 4 and 9). It sounds more like the Bible than the two plain wrong answers and is the longest of the three, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question "Paul says a veil covers something" never says whose. The answers then use "Their hearts," where "their" points back to the Israelites from story card 6, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card tells "Moses' glory faded," which comes from 2 Corinthians 3:7 ("fleeting glory") and 3:13, but the card cites only 2 Corinthians 3:18.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's voice is thin across the walkthrough. Only four story cards carry a joke: the porch light, the dust, the drawer and the sunrise. The rest are plain retellings with no voice, including stop 1 cards 1 and 2 and stop 2 cards 6 and 12. The dust line is mild rather than laugh-out-loud. Most cards read like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
